sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the appellant - Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Limited ["the Insurance Company"], against an award dated 28.08.2008 in Suit No. 100/2007.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: The claim in question arises out of the death of one Mr. Pardeep Shah, in a road accident which took place on 04.03.2007.
The claimants [respondent Nos. 1 to 6 herein] before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal ["the Tribunal"] were his wife, children, and parents.
The owner of the insured vehicle has been arrayed as respondent No. 7 herein.

2. The impugned award dealt with three claims arising out of the same accident, instituted by the present claimants, by the legal heirs of one Mr. Jay Ram Chaurasia [Suit No. 68/2007], who also died in the accident, and one Mr. Upender Rana [Suit No. 75/2007], who was injured in the accident.
The Tribunal held the Insurance Company liable in all three cases, and the Insurance Company appealed all three awards before

4. While issuing notice in the appeal on 29.01.2009, this Court granted stay of execution of the impugned award.
It may be noted that respondent No. 7 was also notified of the present appeal and was, in fact, represented, as recorded in several orders of the Court.

5. After some hearing, Mr. Sameer Nandwani, learned counsel for respondent Nos. 1 to 6 - claimants, submits that the claimants do not wish to press the claims in the present proceedings, but seek liberty to proceed under the erstwhile Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923/ Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 ["the Act"], against respondent No.7.
6.

sentences.text: Mr. Nandwani, therefore, only requests that the right of the claimants, if any, to claim compensation from respondent No. 7 under the Act be reserved.
7. Having regard to the submission of Mr. Nandwani, the appeal is allowed, and the impugned award of the Tribunal in Suit No. 100/2017 is set aside.
This order will not prejudice any rights of the claimants to seek appropriate remedies against respondent No. 7 under the Act, if any.

9. The appeal stands disposed of with these observations.
